dMod2 [@kaschek2019dmod] minimizes $-2 \log L$, with a prior $-2 \log$ of the posterior, by a
trust-region method on the exact gradient, `trust()`, run from many starts by `mstrust()`. The
fits below use the model of [Setting up models](guide-model.html) with the gauge of
[Symmetries](guide-symmetries.html), by `fit.R`, `onefit.R` and `plots.R` of the project.
Derivations: [Methods > Trust-region optimization](methods-trust.html).

## Trust-region method

Each iteration minimizes a quadratic model of the objective inside a ball of radius $r$; the ratio
of actual to predicted decrease decides on the step and the radius. `rinit` is the first radius in
the units of the parameters, on the log scale `0.1` is ten percent of a rate. A trial point at
which the objective fails counts as rejected, so no bounds are needed to keep a fit where the
model can be evaluated. `stepControl$nonmonotone` in $(0, 1)$ also accepts steps that raise the
value; the result is then the best iterate.

`parlower` and `parupper` set bounds. `boundary = "reflective"` (default) keeps the iterates
strictly inside and reports the parameters held by a bound in `atBound`; `boundary = "clip"` takes
them out of the subproblem, runs a single Gauss-Newton phase, reads only `ftol` and `mtol` and stops
with `"fvalue"` or `"iterlim"`.

### Termination criteria

`stopReason` names the test that ended the run:

| `stopReason` | test | `converged` |
|---|---|---|
| `"gradient"` | largest gradient entry, scaled by the distance to a bound, at most `gtol` | `TRUE` |
| `"fvalue"` | an accepted step changed the value by less than `ftol` | `TRUE` |
| `"preddiff"` | predicted decrease below `mtol` | `TRUE` |
| `"step"` | step norm below `xtol` (default 0, off) | `TRUE` |
| `"stagnation"` | five rejected steps in a row, value flat within `ftol` | `TRUE` where the full Newton step predicts at most `mtol` |
| `"radius"` | radius below `rmin`, or a step that no longer changes the parameters | `FALSE` |
| `"objfun"` | three failed evaluations in a row | `FALSE` |
| `"iterlim"` | `iterlim` iterations | `FALSE` |

Only `"gradient"` tests first-order optimality; the last quasi-Newton phase ignores the value,
model and step tests ([Hessian phases](#hessian-phases-and-reverse-sweep)). `"gradient"`,
`"fvalue"` and `"preddiff"` end a run of `trust()` or `trustL1()` only where the full Newton step also predicts a decrease of
at most `mtol` ([Methods > Termination criteria](methods-trust.html#termination-criteria)). `ftol` and `gtol`
belong at or above the numerical error of value and gradient; `model.R` defines them as
`tolerances`, which the fitting scripts pass as `tolControl`.

## Model Hessian

| `hessianMethod` | model Hessian | the objective returns |
|---|---|---|
| `"gn"` | Gauss-Newton | value, gradient, Gauss-Newton Hessian |
| `"exact"` | exact (Newton) | value, gradient, exact Hessian |
| `"bfgs"` | damped BFGS update, positive definite | value, gradient |
| `"sr1"` | symmetric rank-one update, possibly indefinite | value, gradient |

Without `hessianMethod` and `phases`, `trust()` runs the hybrid method of Fides
[@froehlich2022fides]: Gauss-Newton until the radius stayed the same for 20 iterations, then BFGS
from a matrix updated along the Gauss-Newton steps, at the radius of the switch
([Methods > Hessian phases](methods-trust.html#hessian-phases)). A fit that converges before stays
Gauss-Newton; `hessianMethod = "gn"` keeps Gauss-Newton throughout. The sparse path, multiple
shooting and `boundary = "clip"` run Gauss-Newton.

The exact Hessian needs second-order sensitivities, `deriv2 = TRUE` or `derivMode =
"forward-reverse"` ([Sensitivities](guide-sensitivities.html)). The quasi-Newton settings are
entries of `qnControl`:

| entry | default | controls |
|---|---|---|
| `hessianInit` | `"gn"` | seed: Gauss-Newton at the start, `"identity"`, `"exact"`, or for a later BFGS phase `"tracked"`, the BFGS matrix updated along the phases before |
| `hessianReseed` | `"never"` | `"stall"`: reseed at the current iterate instead of stopping on stagnation or on a step that no longer moves it, where the iterate moved since the last reseed, at most eight times per phase |
| `qnMemory` | `0` | `0` accumulates all updates; $m > 0$ rebuilds from the last $m$ pairs |
| `qnCautious` | `1e-8` | cautious test of BFGS; `0` turns it off |
| `qnRejected` | `TRUE` for `"sr1"` | SR1 also updates from rejected trial points |

With `hessianInit = "identity"` the objective needs to return gradients only.

### Hessian phases and reverse sweep

`phases` runs several sources in turn. Each phase is a list with `hessianMethod` and optionally
`iterlim`, `radiusStall`, `sweep`, `keepRadius`, `onStop` and `qnControl`. A phase ends on a value,
model, step or stagnation stop, on the `iterlim` of the phase or after `radiusStall` iterations at
an unchanged radius and hands over to the next; `"gradient"` ends the run, and with
`onStop = "end"` so do the other stops. The next phase starts at `rinit`, or at the radius of the
handover with `keepRadius = TRUE`. `switches` bounds the handovers (default: one fewer than
phases).

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fit <- trust(obj, best, fixed = gauge, tolControl = tolerances,
             phases = list(list(hessianMethod = "gn"), list(hessianMethod = "sr1")))
fit[c("phaseIterations", "evalBySource", "nSwitch", "stopReason")]
```

`sweep = "reverse"` computes the gradient of a quasi-Newton phase by one backward sweep, for models
built with `derivMode = c("forward", "reverse")`; by default a `"bfgs"` or `"sr1"` phase of
`phases` sweeps backwards where it can, while a run without `phases` sweeps only with
`sweep = "reverse"`. With `phases`, `phaseSweep` reports the sweep per phase.

### Sparse Hessians

`sparse = TRUE` solves the subproblem on sparse Cholesky factors of the Hessian, for many
parameters that each act on few conditions; a part of the Hessian that couples many parameters at
once, such as the normalization of an alignment, comes as a low-rank part. The steps, phases,
bounds and stops are those of the dense path, so both reach the same fit. The default `"auto"`
selects the sparse path from 100 parameters on where a step on the sparse Hessian costs fewer
flops than one on the dense Hessian; `options(dMod2.sparseAuto = list(parameters = , fill = ))`
moves the lower bound or replaces the cost by an upper bound of the fill.

### Arguments and result

| argument | default | controls |
|---|---|---|
| `rinit`, `rmax` | `0.1`, `10` | first and largest radius |
| `iterlim` | `1000` | iterations over all phases |
| `hessianMethod` | Gauss-Newton, then BFGS | source of the model Hessian |
| `phases`, `switches` | none | several sources in turn |
| `parlower`, `parupper`, `boundary` | none, `"reflective"` | bounds |
| `tolControl` | `ftol`, `mtol`, `gtol` `1e-6`; `xtol`, `rmin` `0`; `ctol` `1e-6` | termination; `ctol` for multiple shooting |
| `qnControl` | see above | quasi-Newton update |
| `stepControl` | `thetaMax = 0.99995`, `nonmonotone = 0` | step; further entries for multiple shooting |
| `minimize` | `TRUE` | `FALSE` maximizes |
| `sparse` | `"auto"` | sparse path |
| `blather`, `printIter`, `traceFile` | `FALSE`, `FALSE`, none | trace in the result, printed values, CSV log |

Other arguments go to the objective, such as `fixed`. The result, a `trustfit`, holds `argument`,
`value`, `gradient`, `hessian`, `iterations`, `neval`, `converged`, `atBound` and `stopReason`;
with `blather = TRUE` also the path of iterates and trial points. `vcov(fit)` inverts half the
Hessian.


```{r, echo = FALSE}
invisible(stored("results/onefit.rds", "onefit.R"))
```

```{r}
fit <- readRDS("results/onefit.rds")
fit[c("value", "converged", "iterations", "stopReason")]
```

## Multistart fitting

`mstrust()` fits from many starts and returns a list of fits; `as.parframe()` sorts them by value.
`fit.R` draws 200 starts from the prior of [Setting up models](guide-model.html#likelihood-and-prior):

```{r multistart, eval = FALSE}
```

Arguments go by name to `trust()`, to the sampler (`sd` to `rnorm()`) or to the objective. All
starts are drawn before the fits are distributed, so `set.seed()` reproduces a run for any
`cores`.

| argument | default | controls |
|---|---|---|
| `center` | | center of the starts, or a parframe of starts |
| `fits` | `20` | number of fits |
| `samplefun` | `"rnorm"` | sampler of the offsets |
| `startFromCenter` | `FALSE` | first fit starts at `center` |
| `retry`, `nTries` | `TRUE`, `10` | a failed fit restarts from the next draw |
| `cores` | `1` | parallel fits, or `c(fits = , conditions = )` |
| `optmethod` | `"trust"` | optimizer, e.g. `"trustL1"` |
| `output`, `cautiousMode` | `FALSE` | `output` writes every fit to `resultPath/name/trial-<k>-<date>/interRes/` while the run goes on and the parameter list at the end of the run; `cautiousMode` adds a deparsed `.R` copy of every fit, kept after the run |

`msParframe()` draws starts from a separate seed, so several runs can share them; `load.parlist()`
reads the fits in `interRes/` of a run that is still going or was aborted, since a finished run
removes them and leaves `parameterList.Rda`. `helix.R` runs the 200 fits as 100 array tasks
([Remote computing](guide-remote-computing.html)):

```{r, echo = FALSE}
invisible(stored("results/fits.rds", "fit.R"))
```

```{r load}
```

```{r}
c(fits = nrow(fits), converged = sum(fits$converged), best = min(fits$value),
  withinOne = sum(fits$value < min(fits$value) + 1))
```

The waterfall plot shows the sorted values; each plateau is a local optimum, the length of the plateau the size
of the basin of attraction:

```{r waterfall, fig.height = 3.5}
```

The parameters that differ by more than 0.1 between the plateaus within 5 of the best:

```{r}
pl <- plotPars(fits, value < min(value) + 5)
med <- with(pl$data, tapply(parvalue, list(name, step), median))
differ <- rownames(med)[apply(med, 1, function(m) diff(range(m, na.rm = TRUE))) > 0.1]
pl$data <- subset(pl$data, name %in% differ)
```

```{r, fig.height = 1 + 0.22 * length(differ)}
pl +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = rev) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "log value", color = "plateau")
```

## Comparison of Hessian sources

`optimizers.R` fits from the same 100 starts with the default of `trust()`, Gauss-Newton, BFGS and
SR1 on the reverse gradient, the exact Hessian, Gauss-Newton followed by BFGS after 20 iterations or once the
trust-region radius stays unchanged, and the structured methods, which add a learned correction
to the Gauss-Newton Hessian. A task runs at most 30 minutes. `converged`
counts the runs that end on a convergence stop, `hits` the starts that end within 5 of the best
value:

```{r, echo = FALSE}
invisible(stored("results/optimizers.rds", "optimizers.R"))
```

```{r}
opt <- readRDS("results/optimizers.rds")
top <- min(opt$value, na.rm = TRUE)
shown <- c("default (Fides hybrid)", "Gauss-Newton", "BFGS", "exact", "GN, then BFGS", "GN, then BFGS at stall 50", "SSR1, scaled",
           "GNSBFGS")
opt <- opt[opt$method %in% shown, ]
method <- factor(opt$method, shown)
t(rbind(converged = tapply(opt$converged, method, sum),
        hits = tapply(opt$value < top + 5, method, sum, na.rm = TRUE),
        secondsPerHit = round(tapply(opt$elapsed, method, sum, na.rm = TRUE) /
                              tapply(opt$value < top + 5, method, sum, na.rm = TRUE))))
```

A start without a stable resting state is replaced by a draw that has one, as `mstrust()` draws
anew. The exact Hessian converges most often, SR1 with the residual-scaled structured correction
reaches the best plateaus most often, and Gauss-Newton followed by BFGS needs the least time per
hit, since the BFGS phase takes the reverse gradient alone. The default converges more often than
Gauss-Newton at about the same time per hit: half of the default fits stop in the Gauss-Newton
phase, and the BFGS phase takes the forward gradient. Gauss-Newton stops at the iteration limit on plateaus
where the model lacks the curvature of the residuals, and SR1 from the identity needs about as
many iterations as `iterlim` allows. All variants with costs, stops and causes:
[Methods > Forward and reverse derivatives on the Oppelt fit](methods-trust.html#forward-and-reverse-derivatives-on-the-oppelt-fit).

## L1 penalties

`trustL1()` adds $\sum_i \lambda_i \lvert \theta_i - \mu_i \rvert$ for the parameters named in
`mu`, with strength `lambda`. A penalized parameter stays at the reference until the data pull
with a force above $\lambda_i$; a scan over `lambda` selects the parameters that differ.
`one.sided = TRUE` penalizes one side only, `gate` lets parameters leave upward only, `fuse`
penalizes differences within blocks of parameters. Bounds and tolerances are those of `trust()`;
`mstrust(optmethod = "trustL1")` runs it from many starts. Details:
[Methods > L1 penalties](methods-trust.html#l1-penalties).

Multiple shooting, a control of the objective for oscillating or spiking systems, is described
with usage and controls in [Methods > Multiple shooting](methods-multiple-shooting.html).
